title: The $27 List Muhammad Yunus Made in Jobra
conflicts: Recipients: Yunus himself (Nobel lecture 2006, CNN 2007) says 42 people/victims; BBC 2011 says 42 women and the Daily Star 2006 says 42 female basket weavers; the story says 42 people. Gift or loan: 'offered' (lecture), gave and told them to return it (CNN), 'lent' (Daily Star); story says he paid it and told them to return it. Date: lecture ties it to the 1974 famine, BBC and the Magsaysay Foundation give 1976 for the project; story dates the famine and the project, not the $27 itself. Outcome numbers: repayment above 98% (Magsaysay 1984) and 99% (Yunus 2006) vs the Wall Street Journal report (Pearl and Phillips) of 19% of loans overdue, partly disputed by Yunus; borrowers 100,000 (1984), 6.5m (Daily Star 2006), nearly 7.0m (Yunus 2006), 7.3m (Yunus 2007). Story gives claims with speaker and the challenge; WSJ date differs (2001 in references, 2002 per BBC) so it is left undated.
notes: Slate said '42 women' and 'nonprofit'; corrected to 42 people and funding 'mixed' (his own money, then state-bank loans he guaranteed; Grameen is a borrower-owned bank created by ordinance). Quote challenges the founder's 'return the money, be free' with Thoreau on debt. The repeat screen flagged the James Mwangi Equity edition as same-founder but let it through; they are unrelated. Grameen's own websites did not load for the verifier.
